question: Can the 2022 hydroacoustic-seismicity plus spreading-style relation, frozen using a 2020 hydrothermal-vent inventory, prospectively rank hydrothermal systems that were confirmed/discovered later?
why_this_is_special: The source study used Beaulieu and Szafranski 2020 vent data. A 2023 expedition subsequently discovered/confirmed three active hydrothermal vent fields between about 20 and 25 N on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. This creates a natural out-of-time validation opportunity that was not available to the 2022 analysis.

frozen_background_before_validation_scor.source_vent_inventory_cutoff: InterRidge Global Database of Active Submarine Hydrothermal Vent Fields v3.4, Beaulieu & Szafranski 2020

post_cutoff_targets.2023_result: Five active high-temperature black-smoker sites were documented across the summit area; prior work had identified inactive sulfide deposits, so this is not a clean previously-unknown-location test.
Active black smokers were found near the SE base of the massif, about 7 km west of the MAR axis; reported temperatures reached about 338 C.
A vigorously venting high-temperature system was discovered; later descriptions place Hydra on the Grappe Deux non-transform offset and report ultramafic/detachment context.

proposed_blind_rank_metric.purpose: Rank pre-2020 ventless segments without using post-2020 labels.

success_gate: Call this an out-of-time support only if genuinely pre-2020-ventless 2023 discoveries rank materially above the full eligible ventless-segment control population under a metric frozen before looking up their ranks.
failure_gate: If the new fields rank ordinary/low, or were already represented as vent locations in the 2020 inventory, record the result as negative or non-independent and do not rescue the hypothesis by retuning the score.
